To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the most common ENT conditions in the Central Province of the Republic of Kenya are common cold, cough and tonsillitis.
The majority of the plants used in traditional medicine for ENT diseases are herbs, shrubs, trees, and sedges.

(1) the majority of the people interviewed were aware of the existence of traditional remedies for ENT diseases and (2) the most commonly used remedies for these diseases were obtained from plants, and (3) the most frequently used plant species for the treatment of ENT diseases were Eucalyptus sp., Ocimum sp., and Vernonia sp.
In summary, our research is concerned with
documenting and validating the traditional knowledge of the people in the study area.
the identification of plants used for the traditional management of ear, noise and throat diseases in the Central Province of the Kenya.
the documentation of indigenous knowledge of the use of plant species for the management of diseases of ear, nose, and throat in Kenya.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
traditional management of ENT conditions in Central Kenya is based on a large number of plants species.
traditional knowledge and use of medicinal plants is still very important and is being maintained by the local communities of Central Province of Kenya.
traditional medicine is a viable and effective option in management of ENT diseases in this region and hence a potential source for new drug discovery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is an urgent need to conduct ethnobotanical studies in the region to document the plants and the knowledge associated with them.
the majority of the plants used in traditional management of ENT conditions in Central Kenya are of low economic value.
there is a need to document and validate the traditional remedies in order to improve their accessibility to the local communities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
traditional management of ENT diseases in Central Kenya is diverse and complex, and that there is a need for documentation and conservation of these plants for future use.
traditional knowledge of the Central Kenya is a rich repository of information that can be harnessed in the search for new drugs for ENT diseases.
there is a need for further documentation of traditional knowledge of medicinal plants in Kenya and the rest of Africa.
